reason: The cited evidence does not directly address CoCrFeNiTi. E1 discusses nanolamellar AlxCoCuFeNi and ideal plasticity from phase transformation, not low strength from a homogeneous lattice. E2 compares nanoindentation hardness of Al-HEA and Cu-HEA to a CoCrFeMnNi base, attributing differences to alloy chemistry and ideal shear strength, but does not characterize dislocation obstacles or lattice friction in CoCrFeNiTi. The key premises about minimal obstacles and low friction in this specific alloy are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has a homogeneous lattice with few intrinsic obstacles to dislocation motion.
Lack of significant lattice distortions, short-range ordering, or precipitates reduces lattice friction stress and work hardening.
Low lattice friction explains the combination of high plasticity/machinability with low strength.
Introducing nanoscale heterogeneities (twins/precipitates) will impede dislocations and increase strength.
